clue.text: Book place in Cumbria said to be suitable for newlyweds

indicators.note: said to be signals that the place name is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: Rydal is a village in the English Lake District, in Cumbria, home of Wordsworth

explanation.surface: A guidebook entry recommending a Lake District spot as a honeymoon destination.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridal describes anything belonging to a bride or wedding, so it suits a just-married couple.

clue.text: Farmworker's back broken by jerks

indicators.note: broken by says the word for back is split open with the other piece set inside

parts.note: the rear is the back
physical jerks are exercises, i.e. PE (physical education)

explanation.surface: A labourer's spine damaged by sudden wrenching movements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Physical jerks' is a British term for gym exercises, hence PE. The possessive 's in 'Farmworker's' is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A reaper cuts and gathers grain at harvest, a classic farm labourer role.

clue.text: Half-deaf man is in control of car

indicators.note: Half- takes the first two of the four letters of the word deaf

parts.note: a mister is a man, as in a form of address

explanation.surface: A partially deaf driver is the one steering the car.
explanation.definitionFit: A demister is a dashboard control that clears condensation from a car's windows.

clue.text: Yearns to get very reliable bet that could bring big return

definitions.text: bet that could bring big return

parts.note: to long is to yearn
a hot tip or hot favourite is one considered very reliable

explanation.surface: A punter longs for a certainty that will pay out handsomely.
explanation.definitionFit: An outsider's wager at long odds pays a large sum if it comes in.

clue.text: To cowboys, native Americans seemed so embarrassed

definitions.text: To cowboys, native Americans seemed so
definitions.meaning: in Western films the native Americans were called reds, and they faced the cowboys in battle

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the answer as REDS FACED: the cowboys found themselves facing 'reds'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone embarrassed blushes, so the face turns crimson with shame.

clue.text: Girl out of bed that may be served with biscuits

definitions.text: that may be served with biscuits

indicators.note: out of here means the girl's name is outside, wrapped round the bed

parts.note: Rita is a girl's name
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A girl climbing out of bed for a snack.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricotta is a soft Italian cheese, and cheese is often served with crackers or biscuits.

clue.text: Conifers growing wild may be referred to court

indicators.note: growing wild suggests the letters of conifers sprawl into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Untended conifers spreading over a boundary might end in a legal dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: Forensic means relating to courts of law, as with forensic evidence put before a court.

clue.text: Full of ideas, and responsive, putting up chapter

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting up means shifting the letter higher, to the top

parts.note: reactive means responding readily

explanation.surface: An imaginative, responsive author drafting another chapter.
explanation.definitionFit: Creative means inventive, rich in original ideas.

clue.text: Shared expense of delightful trip to tulip fields?

definitions.meaning: an outing where each person pays their own share
a whimsical reading: a lovely treat in Holland, home of the tulip fields

explanation.definitionFit: A meal or outing where everyone pays for themselves is called a going-Dutch arrangement.

clue.text: Tone Phil extracted from orchestra

indicators.note: extracted from says the name Phil is pulled out of the orchestra's word

parts.note: a philharmonic is a symphony orchestra
taken as written

explanation.surface: A musician named Phil being pulled out of the orchestra over his tone.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmonic is an overtone, a secondary tone sounding above the fundamental.

clue.text: Stop what we hear is good equivalent for a change

indicators.note: what we hear is points to a phrase rendered by its sound

parts.note: from the saying 'a change is as good as a rest', so a rest equals a change

explanation.surface: A remark that pausing is just as worthwhile as changing course.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrest something is to halt or check it, as in arresting decline.

clue.text: First-class score against spinner

indicators.note: against means placed next to, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: a top is a toy that spins
to notch is to score, as in notching up runs

explanation.surface: A cricket report of an excellent innings scored against a slow bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface makes 'spinner' look like a slow bowler; it is the toy.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-notch is an idiom for excellent, of the highest quality.

clue.text: Peevish, finishing short note

indicators.note: finishing short says the word for peevish loses its last letter

parts.note: crotchety means irritable or peevish

explanation.surface: An irritable person cutting a message short.
explanation.definitionFit: A crotchet is the British name for a quarter note in music.

clue.text: Fair target makes milk-producer nervous

parts.note: a coconut yields coconut milk
shy means timid or nervous

explanation.surface: A dairy animal made jumpy at a fairground.
explanation.walkthrough: A COCONUT SHY is a British fairground stall where you throw balls to knock coconuts off stands.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a sideshow stall at a funfair where coconuts are the targets.

clue.text: Pecksniff girl shy about her appeal

indicators.note: about means the word for shy goes round the other piece

parts.note: chary means wary or shy
it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A Dickensian young woman too bashful to make her plea.
explanation.walkthrough: Pecksniff is the hypocrite in Dickens's Martin Chuzzlewit; his daughters are Charity and Mercy.
explanation.definitionFit: Charity Pecksniff is one of Mr Pecksniff's two daughters in the Dickens novel.

clue.text: Are travelling, with nothing to prevent one offering a lift

indicators.note: travelling suggests the letters of are move about into a new order

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
to foil is to thwart or prevent

explanation.surface: Travelling by air with nothing to stop you getting a ride.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerofoil is a shaped surface such as a wing that generates lift as air flows over it.

clue.text: Poor country exiling a chap

indicators.note: exiling means sending out, so the letter a is removed

parts.note: India is a country
a gent is a gentleman, a chap

explanation.surface: An impoverished nation deporting a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigent means needy, lacking money and resources.

clue.text: Ship's officer shown around revolutionary cutter

indicators.note: around means the officer's word wraps the other piece

parts.note: a mate is an officer on a merchant ship
Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

explanation.surface: A naval officer showing a radical around the cutter, a type of boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutter' suggests the small sailing vessel the ship's officer might command; it is a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A machete is a broad heavy knife used for cutting through vegetation.

clue.text: John takes grand to America

parts.note: august means grand or venerable
US is the United States of America

explanation.surface: A man named John takes a thousand dollars to the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grand' reads as a thousand in money; it is the adjective. Augustus John was a celebrated Welsh painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Augustus John was the Welsh portrait painter, so his first name pairs with John.

clue.text: Suspended for showing evidence of overindulgence

definitions.meaning: suffering the after-effects of too much drink

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means overhanging; as one it means suffering a morning-after headache.

clue.text: Fall of Roman conspirator extremely desirable

parts.note: Casca was one of the conspirators who stabbed Julius Caesar

indicators.note: extremely takes the extreme letters, first and last, of desirable

explanation.surface: The downfall of a plotter in ancient Rome would be most welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: A cascade is a waterfall, a fall of water over rocks.

clue.text: A journey in sea service, start of trek after gold, for him?

definitions.text: A journey in sea service, start of trek after gold, for him?

indicators.note: after puts the trek letter following the gold symbol
in means the journey word sits inside the service abbreviation

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy
a go can mean a trip or journey, as in a go on the ferry
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: start of takes the first letter of trek

explanation.surface: A sea voyage on a quest for gold: who would go on it?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: the Argonauts sailed with Jason in quest of the Golden Fleece.
explanation.definitionFit: An Argonaut sailed on the Argo seeking the Golden Fleece, a sea trek after gold.

clue.text: One needs all players directed to the same pitch

definitions.text: One needs all players directed to the same pitch

parts.words: One needs all players directed to the same pitch
parts.note: musically, every performer sounding the same note together; 'One' hints at the oneness of the singing

explanation.definitionFit: Singing in unison means every voice produces the same pitch at the same time.

clue.text: Too fond of trouble and strife in the East End?

definitions.text: Too fond of trouble and strife in the East End?

parts.words: Too fond of trouble and strife in the East End?
parts.note: in Cockney rhyming slang of London's East End, trouble and strife means wife, so this is excessive devotion to one's wife

explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble and strife' reads as conflict; Cockney rhyming slang makes it 'wife'.
explanation.definitionFit: Uxorious describes a husband excessively devoted or submissive to his wife.

clue.text: In front of shed, spades and another tool

indicators.note: in front of places the spades letter before the shed word

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for spades in card games
a hovel is a rough shed or hut

explanation.surface: Garden tools laid out in front of a shed.
explanation.walkthrough: In the surface 'shed' is the garden building and spades are digging tools; here spades is the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A shovel is a broad digging tool, a near relative of the spade.

clue.text: Cause promoter to come and see one failing after start of play

parts.note: Act I is the opening of a stage play

indicators.note: failing here means the numeral one drops out of the word

parts.note: to visit is to come and see someone
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A campaigner urged to attend a show after the curtain rises, despite one absence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is a link: ACT I comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An activist campaigns for and promotes a cause.

clue.text: I duly tee off in depths of winter

indicators.note: off suggests the letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A golfer dutifully starting a round in midwinter.
explanation.definitionFit: Yuletide is the Christmas season, which falls in the dark heart of winter.

clue.text: Show intelligence is located around right temple

indicators.note: around means the shine word is placed round the other letter

parts.note: to shine is to show brilliance or cleverness

explanation.surface: Brainpower is found near the right side of the forehead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'temple' looks like the side of the head; it is a sacred place.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrine is a holy place of worship, much like a temple.
